[0] Dating reality shows have long been an extremely popular genre, but Apple TV has never ventured into this space. Although its newly announced series *The Last Person on Earth* is positioned as a "documentary series" rather than a "reality show," it is still the streaming platform's first dating show.

[1] *The Last Person on Earth* will be hosted by renowned couples therapist Esther Perel, and is described as an "innovative experiment."

[2] Perel is a well-known couples therapist and *New York Times* bestselling author who specialises in human relationships.

[3] Perel is also the central figure of Apple TV's newly announced 8-episode dating documentary series *The Last Person on Earth*.

[4] According to the press release: "In the show, seemingly mismatched couples will be carefully matched by Perel and a team of matching experts and therapists, then sent to one of the most romantic and remote destinations on Earth to begin their journey."

[5] It certainly sounds no different from a reality show, just without the negative baggage that comes with the "reality" label. I'd say Apple is trying to give its dating show a more "premium" feel, hence the use of the "documentary series" label.

[8] Apple also announced yesterday that the streaming platform will adapt bestselling author Rebecca Yarros's brand-new romance novel into a TV series. Clearly, the streaming platform is planning to expand its programming beyond core genres such as sci-fi, comedy, and thriller series.

[9] Apple TV costs US$12.99 per month, or can be subscribed at a discounted price through the Apple One bundle.
